learnings.question: Which economist and Nobel laureate first articulated, in 1971, the idea that in an information-rich world, information consumption is fundamentally a matter of consuming the attention of its recipients?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that an information-rich world creates a scarcity of attention, since what information consumes is the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What is the Arabic term, used in Surah Al-Mu'minoon, for the idle talk, gossip, and vain speech that successful believers are described as turning away from?
learnings.learning: Surah Al-Mu'minoon (23:1-3) describes successful believers as those who turn away from Lagw - ill speech, gossip, and meaningless conversation.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist, working in the 1880s, demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus proved that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is the basis of spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What do the researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call the phenomenon where people quickly forget information once they've stored it digitally, treating the save as permission for their brain to delete it?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call this forgetting-after-saving phenomenon Digital Amnesia, a result of the brain treating writing something down as permission to stop remembering it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, what is the name of the artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress by showing remaining work and whether the team is on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three artifacts; it visualizes Sprint progress, shows remaining work, and helps track whether the team is on schedule.

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, what is the primary purpose of breaking the development process into smaller, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To increase the length of the project
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
To eliminate the need for planning
To reduce the number of team members needed
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks work into iterative Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments, rather than locking a team into a long, rigid plan.

learnings.question: What Arabic term, drawn from Quran 2:30, refers to humanity's role as stewards or caretakers of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the term used in Quran 2:30 for humanity's role as a successive authority and caretaker of the Earth, responsible for preserving faith and fostering unity.

learnings.question: In a framework describing human purpose as resting on worship and stewardship of the Earth, what is the third pillar, under which life itself functions as a test of a person's deeds and choices?
options: Pursuing knowledge purely for its own sake
Living life as a test of faith and conduct, with accountability for one's deeds
Building a lasting legacy through one's descendants
learnings.learning: Alongside worship and stewardship (khalifah), life is framed as a test of faith and conduct in which every action is subject to accountability and shapes one's eternal outcome.

learnings.question: Which Prophet, when asked why he exerted himself so much in worship despite his status, is recorded in Sahih Bukhari as having replied, 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'
learnings.learning: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) modeled gratitude as the heart of worship, famously responding to a question about his effort in worship with, 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state is designed for very short durations of idleness, allowing the link to quickly 'wake up' and resume activity, comparable to a computer screen simply turning off?
learnings.learning: L0s is a very light sleep state in PCIe power management, designed for very short idle periods, letting the link wake up quickly to resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power management state represents a device being almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity, giving the highest power savings but the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power state, where the device is almost completely powered down, maximizing power savings for long idle periods at the cost of the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to Allah's complete, eternal, already-written plan for all events, as distinct from the actual unfolding of those events in a person's life?
learnings.learning: Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal plan and knowledge of everything that will happen, while Qada' is the actual unfolding of events as they occur, shaped by a person's actions.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: In a well-known hadith found in Jami at-Tirmidhi, what does Allah do whenever a Muslim sincerely supplicates (makes dua) for something that isn't sinful, if the specific request itself isn't granted?
options: Nothing happens if the same prayer is repeated too often
The request is automatically deferred until the Day of Judgment
Allah turns away from him an equivalent amount of evil
The prayer is simply recorded as a good deed with no further effect
learnings.learning: A hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi states that when a Muslim supplicates for something not sinful, Allah either grants the request or turns away from him an equivalent amount of evil.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: In an 80/20 (Pareto Principle) analysis of word frequency across the Quran's original Arabic text, what percentage of the Quran's total word count do the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: A Pareto-style word-frequency analysis of the Quran's Arabic text found that the top 20 most frequent words account for only about 20.83% of the total word count, not 80% as the Pareto heuristic might suggest.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What is the term for the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate their vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds; without them, reading Arabic accurately becomes much harder.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
